intro_seen.description: Player has seen the waking-on-the-beach narration.

shingle_met_pell.description: Player has met Pell on Shingle Point.

saltmarrow_met_mara.description: Player has met Mara Tollen, the harbormaster.

saltmarrow_mara_told_of_dunstan.description: Mara told the player her brother Dunstan walked into the fog.

saltmarrow_met_aldous.description: Player has met Brother Aldous Wren.

saltmarrow_pebble_fate.description: What the player did with the humming pebble Remnant: '' (not decided), 'given' (to Pell) or 'kept'. Pays off when the Gull's Beacon needs a memory to burn.

saltmarrow_aldous_approach.description: How the player first handled Aldous's evasions: '' / 'gentle' / 'pressed'. Gentle earns his trust (he confides sooner in Act I); pressed makes him defensive.

saltmarrow_hesk_saw_dunstan.description: Old Hesk, Hushed in the net-lofts, told the player a big man with a lantern and 'Tollen shoulders' went north laughing, saying he'd come back for his name.

saltmarrow_mara_knows_dunstan_chose.description: Player told Mara what Hesk saw: Dunstan went into the fog willingly. Pays off when Dunstan is found among the Unmoored (Act II).

saltmarrow_pell_lent_pebble.description: Pell agreed to hand the humming pebble back so the Gull's Beacon could burn it. Stays true even if the player later returns it.

saltmarrow_mara_offered_gull.description: Mara held Dunstan's whittled gull in the fog until it became a Remnant of her memory of him, and gave it to the player for the beacon.

saltmarrow_beacon_burned.description: Which Remnant fed the Gull's Beacon: '' (unlit), 'pebble' (the lullaby — Mara's song, Pell's comfort), 'knot' (Saltmarrow's founding knot) or 'gull' (Mara's memory of her brother Dunstan). The Act I choice; Saltmarrow forgets it for good.

saltmarrow_mara_saw_beacon_lit.description: Player has spoken with Mara after the Gull's Beacon was relit (one-time aftermath scene).

saltmarrow_aldous_balked.description: After the beacon was lit, a player who had not been gentle with Aldous asked for his story; he refused and sent them away. Unlocks showing him the ember on the next visit.

saltmarrow_aldous_confessed.description: Aldous's Act I confession: '' (untold), 'full' (gentle — the High Keeper put the flame out, a light went down the stair past him, gives the Keeper's sleeve-ember) or 'grudging' (pressed — the bare fact only). Keepers in Act II should know which.

saltmarrow_ferry_lantern_hung.description: Mara hung the green signal lantern on the Saltmarrow dock-post so the Tidewright ferry knows passengers are waiting (Act II bridge).

saltmarrow_pell_ferry_ask.description: What the player told Pell about the ferry: '' (not asked), 'promised' (Pell may come), 'refused' (Pell stays; asks for something lost brought back) or 'undecided' (Pell asks again, loudly, when the ferry comes). Asked on seeing the green lantern or on the dock when the ferry is in.

saltmarrow_mara_saw_sleeve_ember.description: Player showed Mara the Keeper's sleeve-ember Aldous cut from his robe; she warned them Tidewrights don't love Keepers.

saltmarrow_ferry_arrived.description: The Tidewright ferry Slow Mercy sounded its horn and put in at the Saltmarrow dock (region arrival event after the green lantern was hung). Pell moves from Shingle Point to the dock.

saltmarrow_ferry_deed.description: How the player told Oda Farrow their deed (the Tidewright fare): '' (not yet), 'claimed' (I relit the Gull), 'shared' (Saltmarrow did; I carried the ember) or 'brusque' (just take me across). Tidewrights in Act II should know how the Wakebearer talks about their deeds.

saltmarrow_oda_knew_dunstan.description: After the gull burn, Oda Farrow (from off-island) spoke of Dunstan Tollen, who crewed for her; the name would not stay with the Wakebearer. Proof that a burned memory survives off the island (Act II payoff).

saltmarrow_oda_saw_sleeve_ember.description: Player showed Oda Farrow the Keeper's sleeve-ember despite Mara's warning; Tidewrights make Keepers pay twice. Act II Tidewrights may be cooler.

saltmarrow_pell_crossing.description: How Pell's wish to cross ended when the ferry came: '' (unresolved), 'aboard' (Mara gave leave; Pell crosses on the Slow Mercy), 'stayed' (Pell stays and gave the player a finding pouch) or 'let_down' (promised, then the player told Mara Pell should stay). Act II must honour it.

saltmarrow_mara_farewell.description: Mara said goodbye to the player after the ferry's horn (one-time scene).

saltmarrow_mara_message_for_dunstan.description: Mara, knowing Dunstan chose the fog, asked the player to tell him the stool is still there, if they see him. Pays off when Dunstan is found among the Unmoored (Act II).

saltmarrow_ferry_passage.description: Oda Farrow gave the player a berth on the Slow Mercy for Thornwold, sailing on the evening tide. Ends Act I (the act-end card); Act II starts from it.

lanes_ferry_at.description: Where the Slow Mercy lies after the crossing: '' (not sailed yet: at the Saltmarrow dock once arrived), 'thornwold' (moored at Thornwold landing), 'saltmarrow' (back at the Saltmarrow dock) or 'fen' (at Glasswater Fen's staithe, Day 29). Oda and the ferry prop are placed by it; the player travels with her.

thornwold_landed.description: The player has come ashore at Thornwold landing (one-time arrival scene after the crossing).

thornwold_pell_landed.description: Pell crossed on the Slow Mercy (saltmarrow_pell_crossing=aboard) and stays at Thornwold's lumber camp, sorting Bram's nails. Moves Pell off the Saltmarrow dock.

thornwold_met_bram.description: Player has met Bram Kettle, foreman of the Tidewright lumber camp at Thornwold landing.

thornwold_bram_knot_grudge.description: Bram Kettle (Saltmarrow-born mother, Tidewright) holds the burning of the founding knot against the player. Tidewright net-makers' resentment of the knot burn (LORE); later Tidewrights may share it.

thornwold_bramble_parted.description: The Wakebearer held the ember to the bramble wall and the canes drew back from it, opening a gap onto the cart road behind. The way into the woods past the wall (through the bramble wall's dialogue).

thornwold_woods_entered.description: Player has seen the arrival scene in the woods past the bramble wall (one-time).

thornwold_met_hob.description: Player has met Hob Marl, the last collier on the near side of the ridge, in the clearing past the bramble wall. He brings the sacks down by the lanterns.

thornwold_hob_stick.description: Player told Hob Marl that Pell found a tally stick by the sacks; it is his ('the night I forgot what I was counting') and he lets Pell keep it. Pell can be told whose it is.

thornwold_hob_paid.description: Player carried Bram's salt crock to Hob Marl: the colliers' first pay since the third load. Bram's tally board gets its fourth salt notch and Hob remembers Bram.

thornwold_ladder_stood.description: The Wakebearer stood the Keepers' fallen ladder back against the last pitch above the stair's landing in the woods. The way up to the ridge (climbing it travels to thornwold_ridge).

thornwold_ridge_reached.description: Player has seen the arrival scene on Thornwold's ridge (one-time, after first climbing the ladder).

thornwold_met_lamp.description: Player has met the Lamp at the lantern bench by the keeper's lodge on the ridge (advances A Light for Thornwold to the_lamp).

thornwold_lamp_coal_told.description: The Lamp showed the player what is in the iron box: the last coal of the Spire's midwinter fire, broken into slivers for the waymark lanterns. When it is spent the lanterns go out.

thornwold_lamp_name_lost.description: The Lamp told the player it had another name once and 'put it somewhere' (forgotten). A Remnant candidate for the Ridge Light's burning.

thornwold_lamp_ladder_told.description: The Lamp admitted putting the ladder down after the fourth collier came up asking for a lantern, so there would be no fifth. The four went on north along the ridge.

thornwold_lamp_heard_of_aldous.description: Player told the Lamp what Brother Aldous confessed in Saltmarrow (reads saltmarrow_aldous_confessed; the Lamp recognises the sleeve-ember's stitching if the player carries it). The coal in the iron box went cold on one side the night of the Snuffing.

thornwold_stair_light.description: What the player asked of the Lamp for the dark Keepers' stair: '' (not asked), 'sliver' (the Lamp broke a new sliver off the last coal - it shrinks), 'moved' (take the fourth waymark's lantern off the colliers' road - Hob's road gets darker) or 'refused' (the stair stays dark). Shifting paths: the woods' light follows the choice.

thornwold_fourth_lantern_taken.description: The player unhooked the lantern from the fourth waymark on the colliers' road (thornwold_stair_light=moved): that waymark goes dark and its pool of clear ground closes up.

thornwold_stair_lantern_hung.description: The player hung a Keeper's lantern on the bare waymark at the foot of the Keepers' stair (taking down the collier's cap that hung there): the stair stands in clear light.

thornwold_hob_has_cap.description: Player gave Hob Marl the felt cap from the stair's waymark: Ottie Swale's, one of the four colliers who went up after the Lamp. Hob keeps it on the cold hut's seat with the boots. Once Hob gives the boots away (thornwold_boots_away) the cap goes with them.

thornwold_boots_away.description: Hob Marl gave Ottie Swale's boots (and the cap, if he had it) to the player as a Remnant of his memory of the four colliers, for the Ridge Light. The cold hut's seat is bare while it is true; returning the unburned boots sets it false again. Stays true if they are burned.

thornwold_salt_row_away.description: Bram Kettle unpegged the SALT row from his tally board and made it a Remnant of the camp's memory of the colliers, for the Ridge Light. The board's bottom pegs are bare while it is true; returning the unburned stick sets it false again. Stays true if it is burned.

thornwold_beacon_burned.description: Which Remnant fed the Ridge Light: '' (unlit), 'boots' (Hob Marl's memory of the four colliers who went up after the Lamp — he stops waiting, the cold hut is nobody's) or 'salt_row' (the lumber camp's memory of the colliers and the salt trade — the camp will never know who brings the charcoal). Thornwold's burning; Thornwold forgets it for good.

thornwold_hob_came_in.description: After the Ridge Light was lit, a paid Hob Marl kept his promise and came in to the lumber camp by daylight (one-time arrival scene at the landing). Moves Hob from the clearing to the camp; Bram knows him unless the salt row burned.

thornwold_lamp_saw_light.description: Player has spoken with the Lamp after the Ridge Light was lit (one-time aftermath: the lanterns can go out now; what the coal is kept for).

fen_landed.description: The player has come ashore at Glasswater Fen's staithe (one-time arrival scene after the first sailing north-about from Thornwold).

fen_met_hesper.description: Player has met Hesper Vail, Unmoored warden of Stillhithe's staithe.

fen_ember.description: Asked by Hesper to cup the ember on Stillhithe ('it reminds'): 'cupped' (closed their hand over it) or 'bare' (refused). The Unmoored react to it.

fen_heard_of_dunstan.description: Hesper told the player about the big man who rowed to the fen, paid his mooring in whittled gulls, left his name with her and went out along the long walk into the Deeps. Starts The Letting Post.

fen_rowboat_seen.description: Player has looked at the Saltmarrow rowboat tied at Glasswater's staithe (Oda can then name its builder).

fen_dunstan_word.description: What the player left on the Unmoored's letting post for the big man further in: 'mara' (Mara's word: the stool's still by the door), 'own' (someone from Saltmarrow came looking) or 'none' (left nothing: the right to forget). Pays off when Dunstan is found.

fen_hesper_saw_word.description: Hesper has remarked on what the player left (or didn't) on the letting post (one-time).

fen_met_corran.description: Player has met Corran Teal, the last of the fen folk, at his eel landing.

fen_corran_trap_asked.description: Asked again to be poled out to the Heron, Corran sent the player to lift his far trap at the end of the long walk, in the Deeps' fog, where he won't walk (he doesn't go where the Unmoored go).

fen_corran_decided.description: Corran has decided he likes the player (they lifted his far trap and brought it back; in it, the keeper's skiff bell) and will pole them out to the Heron Light.

fen_punt_out.description: The player is out at the Heron Light's legs in Corran's punt (Corran is there with them, not at his landing). Cleared when he poles them back.

fen_heron_reached.description: Corran has poled the player out through the channels to the Heron Light's legs at least once (the first trip is the full scene).

fen_dunstan_glimpsed.description: At the Heron's legs the player saw a big man with an unlit lantern standing at the edge of the fog on a tussock, looking at the water, before he walked off into it: 'called' (called his name; he stopped, didn't turn, went on), 'watched' (let him go without a word) or 'nameless' (after the gull burn: his name wasn't there to call). Pays off when Dunstan is found.

fen_skiff_bell.description: What the player did with the keeper's skiff bell Corran found in his far trap, at her skiff by the Heron's legs: 'hung' (tied it back on her bow) or 'kept' (kept it). For The Heron Light, part two.

fen_heron_ladder_seen.description: Player has looked at the Heron Light's ladder: the rungs above the slime scraped clean by boots, recently. Someone climbs it (open; part two).
